title: Six-Figure Employees
description:
Report the `name` and `salary` of every employee earning **more than 100000**.

Name the columns `name` and `salary`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000;
hint: A plain WHERE filter. Remember that comparisons against NULL are never true — a NULL salary is not > 100000.
outputExplanation: Ava ($150k), Ben ($120k), Cara ($120k) and Eve ($130k) earn more than $100,000. Dan, Finn, Gia and Hal earn $100k or less.

title: Headcount Per Department
description:
Report every department name and how many employees it has. Departments with **no employees** must still appear, with a count of 0.

Name the columns `department` and `employees`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS employees
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name;
hint: COUNT(*) would count the NULL row a LEFT JOIN produces for an empty department. Count a column from the right table instead.
outputExplanation: Engineering has 4 employees, Sales has 3 and HR has 1.

title: Department Payroll
description:
Report each department's name and its total salary bill. A department with no employees (or only NULL salaries) must report `0`, not NULL.

Name the columns `department` and `payroll`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary), 0) AS payroll
FROM departments d
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name;
hint: SUM over no rows is NULL, not 0. Wrap it in COALESCE or IFNULL.
outputExplanation: Engineering's total payroll is $485,000, Sales is $285,000, and HR is $60,000.

title: How Many Of Each Title
description:
Report each job title and the number of employees holding it, but only for titles held by **two or more** people.

Name the columns `title` and `headcount`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY title
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hint: Filtering on an aggregate is HAVING, not WHERE.
outputExplanation: Three employees are Engineers, two are Managers, and two are Reps. Analyst is held by only one person and is not reported.
